frequency_question: How often is a complex industrial subsidy or credit-guarantee scheme fully drafted, inter-ministerially cleared, legally vetted, and formally gazetted within a 9.5-month (287 days) window, assuming total political and bureaucratic cooperation?
membership_rule: Includes: major national-level sector-specific financial incentive schemes involving budgetary outlays and credit guarantees by a federal ministry. Excludes: minor administrative circulars, emergency decrees, or simple extensions of existing schemes.

cases.name: FAME-II Scheme Notification (Phase 2 of Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles)
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage
National Green Hydrogen Mission Implementation Guidelines
PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme Guidelines and Notification

coverage_note: 5 well-documented major federal industrial schemes examined; estimated total of ~10 comparable federal schemes in this specific window.
known_gaps: Excludes minor state-level schemes or schemes pushed through under emergency pandemic ordinance powers.
skeleton: Decomposed into sequential administrative phases: 1) Inter-ministerial consultation (Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Law) taking 90 days; 2) Cabinet/Empowered Group of Ministers approval taking 60 days; 3) Financial outlay structuring and bank/NAB/SIDBI guarantee framework design taking 60 days; 4) Final gazette notification and drafting taking 45 days. Total minimum sequential time = 255 days.
multiplier: 255 baseline physical process days + 32 days contingency buffer vs 287 days available window
validity_reason: Bureaucratic procedures, standard inter-ministerial consultation workflows, and legal vetting requirements remain stable under current administrative law frameworks.
